title: Two pregnant women (Luke 1:39–45)
hookLine: Mary hurries to her cousin Elizabeth, and the baby in Elizabeth's womb leaps

lines: THE ONE WHO'D JUST GET IT.
cards: Mary has news she can't explain to anyone at home. Some news needs one person who'll just get it. Mary has one.
The angel mentioned her: Elizabeth, her older relative, married to a priest called Zacharias, the woman people had written off as unable to have children, now six months pregnant.

So Luke says Mary gets up and goes with haste into the hill country of Judah, a long way south of Nazareth, walking to the one house where someone might understand. She reaches the door and calls out a greeting.
Before she can say another word, something happens inside Elizabeth.

teach.h: THE BABE LEAPED IN HER WOMB.
teach.b: When Elizabeth hears Mary's greeting, Luke says, "the babe leaped in her womb." Filled with the Holy Spirit, Elizabeth cries out with a loud voice: "Blessed art thou among women, and blessed is the fruit of thy womb."

teach.h: SHE KNEW BEFORE SHE WAS TOLD.
teach.b: Mary hasn't told her anything. No explaining, no convincing. Elizabeth already knows.

teach.h: WHO AM I, THAT YOU'D COME TO ME?
teach.b: Then she asks a question that sounds almost embarrassed: "And whence is this to me, that the mother of my Lord should come to me?" Who am I, that you'd come to me?
The older woman, the priest's wife, honoring the young woman from the small town. As soon as your greeting reached my ears, she says, "the babe leaped in my womb for joy."

That baby grows up to be John the Baptist, the wild man by the river we'll meet in a few weeks. Some readers see this as the first time anyone in Luke recognizes Jesus, and it's a child not yet born, leaping.

Joy recognizing joy. Elizabeth ends with a blessing, not for the baby this time, but for Mary herself: "blessed is she that believed." This visit is the Visitation, with its own feast day in the Western church calendar.
Elizabeth's words later joined Gabriel's greeting in the Hail Mary, the prayer Catholics say, and in the Orthodox hymn to Mary that begins with the angel's rejoice.
Luke adds one small detail: Mary stays about three months.
Two women, one old and one young, both carrying something they didn't expect, keeping each other company until the time comes.

how: Many churches keep the Feast of the Visitation (May 31 in the Catholic calendar). Catholics say Elizabeth's greeting every time they pray the Hail Mary; Christian art often paints the two women embracing at the door.

o: a shepherd's visit to a lambing pen
Mary's visit to Elizabeth, both expecting
a priest's visit to bless a new home

games.q: who said or did what — tap the pairs.
p: went into the hill country with haste

s: Mary told Elizabeth her news before Elizabeth blessed her
Mary only greets her. Elizabeth knows before anything is explained.
the baby who leaped grew up to be John the Baptist
Elizabeth's son is John, the wild man by the river.
Luke says she stayed about three months (Luke 1:56).

games.q: you're Elizabeth, old, pregnant at last. your young relative from Nazareth appears at the door and calls out a greeting. what do you do?
o: ask her what brings her so far.
cry out a blessing, because you already know.
send her home to her family.
games.why: the baby leaps, and Elizabeth cries out: blessed art thou among women. she asks, who am I, that the mother of my Lord should come to me?

practice: Let your shoulders drop and think of the person who'd understand, not fix it, just understand: someone who's been through something like it, or knows you well enough that you needn't explain.
Hold their face a few breaths and notice what it feels like to be known without explaining. If you pray, you can hold them in your prayer; if you don't, just let yourself be glad they exist.

wordCard.voice: Visitation. The name for this meeting between Mary and Elizabeth, the young woman and the old one, and the baby who leaped for joy before a word was explained.

orig.note: Greek: it leaped, it skipped, like a young animal in a field. Luke's word for the baby in Elizabeth's womb.

carryVoice: Your line: joy knows joy. Elizabeth knew before Mary said a word. See you tomorrow.
